problem:
Prove that if $n$ is an odd integer, then $7n+4$ is odd.

Let $n$ be an odd integer. Then, $n=\,${{field-1}} for some integer $a.$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}7n+4 & ={{field-2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $b=$ {{field-3}}. Since $a$ is {{field-4}}, we have that $b$ is {{field-5}}.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}7n+4 & ={{field-6}}\end{aligned}
$$

which is one larger than a multiple of $2.$ Therefore, $7n+4$ is {{field-7}}.
